_meta.status: DEMO ONLY - hand-curated, small, not a clinical reference
_meta.replace_with: A licensed, versioned terminology + interaction source (e.g. RxNorm for names; a licensed DDI dataset such as DrugBank or First Databank for interactions). See PRD section 18 / tech stack 'Medication verification: NEEDS SELECTION'.
_meta.rule: A medicine not listed here is reported as 'cannot confirm'. An interaction is only reported as found when the pair is listed here. Absence of a pair is NOT evidence of safety.

interactions.description: Both are P2Y12 antiplatelet medicines. Taking both is usually a duplication and can raise the risk of bleeding.
Together they raise the risk of bleeding. Doctors sometimes prescribe this pair on purpose for a set time.

Both are statins for cholesterol. Usually only one statin is used; taking two may raise the risk of muscle problems.
Both are beta-blockers. Together they may slow the heart rate or lower blood pressure too much.
Beta-blockers can hide some warning signs of low blood sugar.

NSAIDs like naproxen can weaken the blood pressure effect of lisinopril and can affect the kidneys.
Two NSAID-type medicines together can raise the risk of stomach bleeding.
